Natural_Language: This part prescribes policies and procedures for consent to subcontracts or advance notification of subcontracts, and for review and approval of contractors' purchasing systems. The consent and advance notification requirements of subpart 44.2 do not apply to prime contracts for commercial products or commercial services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_44_000: Scope of Part 44 covers subcontracting policies, consent/advance notification, and purchasing system review/approval
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for Part 44 scope. Two subsections define affirmative scope and exclusion respectively.

Natural_Language: This part prescribes policies and procedures for consent to subcontracts or advance notification of subcontracts, and for review and approval of contractors' purchasing systems.
Atomic_Propositions: P_44_000_a_1: Part 44 prescribes policies and procedures for consent to subcontracts or advance notification of subcontracts; P_44_000_a_2: Part 44 prescribes policies and procedures for review and approval of contractors' purchasing systems
Validation_Notes: Declarative scope statement. Part 44 covers two distinct areas: (1) subcontract consent/advance notification and (2) purchasing system review/approval. Both are conjunctive requirements of the part's coverage.

Natural_Language: The consent and advance notification requirements of subpart 44.2 do not apply to prime contracts for commercial products or commercial services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_44_000_b_1: Prime contract is for commercial products or commercial services; P_44_000_b_2: Consent and advance notification requirements of subpart 44.2 apply
Validation_Notes: Exclusionary provision. If the prime contract is for commercial products or commercial services, then the consent/advance notification requirements of subpart 44.2 are negated. Uses HIGH-RISK Rule 15 because the implication establishes a categorical exemption. Real-world interpretation: commercial prime contracts are entirely exempt from subpart 44.2 consent and notification requirements.

Natural_Language: Definitions as used in this part.
Atomic_Propositions: P_44_001: Definitions applicable to Part 44 consist of Contractor, CPSR, Subcontract, and Subcontractor
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for Part 44 definitions section. Four definitions collectively establish terminology for the part.

Natural_Language: Contractor means the total contractor organization or a separate entity of it, such as an affiliate, division, or plant, that performs its own purchasing.
Atomic_Propositions: P_44_001_a: Contractor is the total contractor organization or a separate entity (affiliate, division, or plant) that performs its own purchasing
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement. Already atomic. Defines contractor broadly to include organizational subunits that manage their own purchasing.

Natural_Language: Contractor purchasing system review (CPSR) means the complete assessment of a contractor's purchasing of material and services, subcontracting, and subcontract management from developing the requirement through completing subcontract performance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_44_001_b: CPSR is the complete assessment of contractor's purchasing of material and services, subcontracting, and subcontract management from requirement development through subcontract performance completion
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement. Already atomic. Establishes CPSR as a comprehensive end-to-end assessment covering the full subcontracting lifecycle.

Natural_Language: Subcontract means any contract as defined in subpart 2.1 entered into by a subcontractor to furnish supplies or services for performance of a prime contract or a subcontract. It includes but is not limited to purchase orders, and changes and modifications to purchase orders.
Atomic_Propositions: P_44_001_c_1: Subcontract is any contract as defined in subpart 2.1 entered into by a subcontractor to furnish supplies or services for performance of a prime contract or a subcontract; P_44_001_c_2: Subcontract includes but is not limited to purchase orders and changes and modifications to purchase orders
Validation_Notes: Two-part definition: core definition referencing subpart 2.1, and an expansive inclusion clause for purchase orders and their modifications. Conjunction appropriate as both aspects define the term.

Natural_Language: Subcontractor means any supplier, distributor, vendor, or firm that furnishes supplies or services to or for a prime contractor or another subcontractor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_44_001_d: Subcontractor is any supplier, distributor, vendor, or firm furnishing supplies or services to or for a prime contractor or another subcontractor
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement. Already atomic. Broad definition covering any entity in the supply chain.

Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for section 44.201. Five subsections collectively address consent and advance notice requirements.

Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for consent requirements. Two subsections address approved vs. non-approved purchasing system scenarios.

Natural_Language: If the contractor has an approved purchasing system, consent is required for subcontracts specifically identified by the contracting officer in paragraph (d) of 52.244-2, Subcontracts. The contracting officer may require consent to subcontract to protect the Government because of the subcontract type, complexity, or value, or because the subcontract needs special surveillance.

Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18

The second sentence uses 'may' creating discretionary authority for the CO to require additional consent for government protection purposes. Tautology represents CO discretion. HIGH-RISK Rule 15 used for the conditional trigger.

Natural_Language: Under cost-reimbursement contracts, the contractor is required by statute to notify the contracting officer as follows:

Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for advance notification. Introductory text establishes cost-reimbursement context. Two subsections distinguish defense/NASA and civilian agency statutory requirements.

Natural_Language: For the Department of Defense, the Coast Guard, and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, unless the contractor maintains an approved purchasing system, 10 U.S.C. 3322(c) requires notification before the award of any cost-plus-fixed-fee subcontract, or any fixed-price subcontract that exceeds the greater of the simplified acquisition threshold or 5 percent of the total estimated cost of the contract.

Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Disjunction (Disj): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Complex conditional with conjunctive antecedent and disjunctive subcontract type trigger. Three conditions must be met: (1) DoD/CG/NASA contract, (2) no approved purchasing system, AND (3) either CPFF subcontract or FP subcontract exceeding threshold. The 'unless' clause for approved purchasing system creates the negation condition. Statutory cite to 10 U.S.C. 3322(c). HIGH-RISK Rule 15 for multi-factor conditional.

Natural_Language: For civilian agencies other than the Coast Guard and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, even if the contractor has an approved purchasing system, 41 U.S.C. 3905 requires notification before the award of any cost-plus-fixed-fee subcontract, or any fixed-price subcontract that exceeds either the simplified acquisition threshold or 5 percent of the total estimated cost of the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_44_201_2_b_1: Contract is with a civilian agency other than Coast Guard or NASA; P_44_201_2_b_2: Subcontract is cost-plus-fixed-fee; P_44_201_2_b_3: Subcontract is fixed-price and exceeds either SAT or 5 percent of total estimated cost; P_44_201_2_b_4: Contractor provides notification to CO before subcontract award
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Disjunction (Disj): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Complex conditional similar to (a) but notably broader: approved purchasing system status is irrelevant for civilian agencies ('even if'). Statutory cite to 41 U.S.C. 3905. Also note the threshold difference from (a): civilian uses 'either...or' (disjunctive threshold) while defense uses 'greater of' (selecting higher threshold). This means civilian threshold is lower and triggers more frequently. HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement ('must'). Three conjunctive obligations: review the data, assess risk appropriateness, and verify policy/business judgment consistency. Reference to Part 42 for delegation authority noted.

Natural_Language: Withholding or withdrawing approval.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must withhold or withdraw approval of a contractor's purchasing system when major weaknesses exist or when the contractor is unable to provide enough information upon which to make an affirmative determination. The contracting officer may withdraw approval at any time based on a determination that the contractor's purchasing system has deteriorated or to protect the Government's interest.
Atomic_Propositions: P_44_301_5_a_1: Major weaknesses exist in purchasing system; P_44_301_5_a_2: Contractor unable to provide sufficient information for affirmative determination; P_44_301_5_a_3: CO withholds or withdraws purchasing system approval; P_44_301_5_a_4: CO determines purchasing system has deteriorated or Government interest needs protection
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Disjunction (Disj): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Two-part provision: mandatory withholding/withdrawal when major weaknesses or insufficient info (first sentence, 'must'), and discretionary withdrawal for deterioration or Government interest (second sentence, 'may'). Tautology for the discretionary element. HIGH-RISK Rule 15.

Natural_Language: When approval is withheld or withdrawn, the contracting officer must notify the contractor in writing within 10 days after completing the review. The notice must specify the deficiencies that must be corrected to qualify the system for approval and request the contractor to furnish within 15 days a plan to correct the deficiencies. If the plan is accepted, the contracting officer must make a follow-up review as soon as the contractor notifies the contracting officer that the deficiencies have been corrected.
Atomic_Propositions: P_44_301_5_b_1: Approval is withheld or withdrawn; P_44_301_5_b_2: CO notifies contractor in writing within 10 days of completing review; P_44_301_5_b_3: Notice specifies deficiencies to be corrected; P_44_301_5_b_4: Notice requests contractor to furnish correction plan within 15 days; P_44_301_5_b_5: Contractor's correction plan is accepted; P_44_301_5_b_6: Contractor notifies CO that deficiencies are corrected; P_44_301_5_b_7: CO makes follow-up review
Validation_Notes: Two-stage conditional. First: withholding/withdrawal triggers mandatory notification with specified contents and timeline (10 days, 15 days). Second: accepted plan plus contractor notification of correction triggers mandatory follow-up review. Both use 'must'. HIGH-RISK Rule 15.
